_comment: Order matters and it is not the obvious way round: where two rules
match one file, the LAST one wins. So the broad globs go first and
Default is no-cache for everything, which does not mean 'do not
store' — it means 'ask before using'. Repeat visits get a 304 and
a few hundred bytes, and a deploy reaches a phone on the next
launch rather than whenever an expiry happens to lapse.
That default is the whole point. The service worker is
network-first so a redeploy shows up immediately, but its fetch()
goes through the browser's HTTP cache like anyone else's — so a
max-age on the app's own files silently overrides the strategy,
and the worker faithfully serves back whatever the cache handed
it. app.css was on a week; the shell at / was on an hour.
